<reflection>
The first experiment provided a kinetic profile that many mechanisms fit with very similar negative log-likelihood (NLL) values, indicating poor discrimination. The NLL differences among the top mechanisms are less than 0.5, while M20 is noticeably worse. The aim of obtaining initial data was achieved, but the results highlight the need for a more informative experiment to distinguish between the many plausible mechanisms.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
Adding initial product will probe reversibility and product-dependent steps, which vary across mechanisms. Mechanisms with reversible catalytic steps (e.g., M1, M2, M3) will exhibit a decreased net forward rate due to reverse reaction. Mechanisms with product-induced deactivation (M12, M17) may show accelerated catalyst loss, leading to faster rate decay. Mechanisms without product inhibition or with different product interactions will respond differently. By keeping substrate and catalyst concentrations identical to the first experiment, we isolate the effect of product, enabling direct comparison. This design is effective because it perturbs the system in a manner sensitive to a wide range of mechanisms, including those with reversible steps, product inhibition, and product-dependent deactivation, without using extreme conditions that could collapse mechanistic differences.
</hypothesis>
